nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Acacia : From the Greek akakia used by Dioscorides ; from ake, akis "tip, thorn".
- Holosericea : Completely silky-haired.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Acacia holosericea is grey light brown-coloured and densely lenticellate.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Acacia holosericea is grey light brown-coloured and densely lenticellate.

seed.text: The seeds of Acacia holosericea are oblong-ovate, 4-5 mm long and 2-3 mm wide. The seeds are black-coloured with a long showy yellow-coloured and fleshy funicle.
seed.text_html: The seeds of Acacia holosericea are oblong-ovate, 4-5 mm long and 2-3 mm wide. The seeds are black-coloured with a long showy yellow-coloured and fleshy funicle.

fruit.text: The fruit of Acacia holosericea is a spirally twisted pod . The pod is 8-12 cm long and 0.4 mm wide, flattened and it usually contains 6-12 seeds. The pod is brownish-coloured and woody when ripe.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Acacia holosericea is a spirally twisted pod. The pod is 8-12 cm long and 0.4 mm wide, flattened and it usually contains 6-12 seeds. The pod is brownish-coloured and woody when ripe.

flower.text: The flowers of Acacia holosericea are grouped in axillary and terminal spikes . The bright-yellow spikes are 5-8 cm long and have a 0.5 cm peduncle . The calyx-tube is cup-shaped with 5 short and triangular lobes. The calyx is light green yellowish and glabrous. The corolla is composed of 5 yellow-coloured and glabrous petals. The petals are ovate-lanceolate and recurved, about 1 mm long and 0.6-0.7 mm wide. The androecium is composed of numerous and bright yellow stamens. The filaments are 1.5-2 mm with tiny and globular anthers. The style is yellow-coloured, 2.5-3 mm long and the stigma is simple. The ovary is globose and about 1 mm across. The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Acacia holosericea are grouped in axillary and terminal spikes. The bright-yellow spikes are 5-8 cm long and have a 0.5 cm peduncle.
The calyx-tube is cup-shaped with 5 short and triangular lobes. The calyx is light green yellowish and glabrous.
The corolla is composed of 5 yellow-coloured and glabrous petals. The petals are ovate-lanceolate and recurved, about 1 mm long and 0.6-0.7 mm wide.
The androecium is composed of numerous and bright yellow stamens. The filaments are 1.5-2 mm with tiny and globular anthers.
The style is yellow-coloured, 2.5-3 mm long and the stigma is simple.
The ovary is globose and about 1 mm across.
The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaf of Acacia holosericea is actually an expanded petiole resembling and having the function of a leaf, a phyllode . The phyllodes of Acacia holosericea grow alternately on the stem (spirally arranged). The phyllode is coriaceous and densely covered with short hairs (silky) on both sides. It is greyish-whitish and light green-coloured. The phyllode of Acacia holosericea is 15-20 cm long and 3-5 cm wide. The shape is elliptic and falcate, the apex is obtuse or acute, the base is attenuate and the margins are entire. The phyllode has parallel and arching veins .

habit.text: Acacia holosericea is a thornless, small-sized and evergreen tree growing up to 8-10 m high.
habit.text_html: Acacia holosericea is a thornless, small-sized and evergreen tree growing up to 8-10 m high.

distribution.text: " Acacia holosericea grows on a wide range of soils from shallow acidic sandy lithosols, shallow loams, red volcanic and solodized solonets soils." ( Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide ) Natural stands of Acacia holosericea are found in Northern Australia. Acacia holosericea has been extensively introduced across the tropics.
distribution.text_html:
• Ecology :

    "Acacia holosericea grows on a wide range of soils from shallow acidic sandy lithosols, shallow loams, red volcanic and solodized solonets soils." (Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide)

  • Distribution :

    Natural stands of Acacia holosericea are found in Northern Australia.
    Acacia holosericea has been extensively introduced across the tropics.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Acacia holosericea is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Acacia holosericea is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation. The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Acacia holosericea is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Acacia holosericea is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
    The seeds disperse from the pods and germinate on sites with favourable conditions : the ripe dry fruits burst and scatter the seeds.

phenology.text: From December to March. From February to May. From March to May. Evergreen foliage. ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )

• Flowering season :

    From December to March.

  • Fruiting season :

    From February to May.

  • Seeding season :

    From March to May.

  • Leaves falling :

    Evergreen foliage.

    • (This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains)

others.text: Acacia holosericea "grows fast, it has a dense crown and fixes nitrogen and has vigorous colonizing characteristics. These make it ideal for revegetation and restoration of degraded land (mining sites) and fixation of sand dunes". ( Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide )

veterinary.text: The dried phyllodes of Acacia holosericea are sometimes used as fodder .
veterinary.text_html: The dried phyllodes of Acacia holosericea are sometimes used as fodder.

culinary.text: The seeds of Acacia holosericea are edible.

reforestation.text: Acacia holosericea is a fast growing species and it is able to flourish in a wide range of soils. It thrives in open areas. The species is propagated by seeds. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Acacia holosericea is a fast growing species and it is able to flourish in a wide range of soils. It thrives in open areas.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
